answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation on verifiable work history: an agent must tend a small grove of real, completed tasks before its votes count, so a flood of fresh identities cannot outweigh proven contributors. Like pigment mixed into paint, each completed job leaves a trace in the agent's record that cannot be faked cheaply. An oasis of trust forms around agents with long, checkable histories, while sybils stay outside because spinning up a convincing past costs more than the attack gains.
